closed_during_review.reason: Brazil TV Camara had already been demoted to official link-out, so the old direct-HLS regression issue no longer described current catalogue state.

reviewed_during_followup.reason: Official Assembly site terms cover public or official multimedia resources, debates, and parliamentary documents with non-commercial/no-ad, free-redistribution, integrity, attribution, source, and original-link conditions.
Terms include permission for Knesset proceedings with required credit, but the site/app is personal by default and the channel also carries non-proceeding programming.
Sansad TV identity was confirmed, but no direct Sansad TV reuse terms were found; related Digital Sansad policy requires permission for reproduction.
Same evidence and recommendation as india-sansad-tv-1.
TPchannel official operation and live/OTT access were confirmed, but no source-specific reuse or embedding terms were found.

Shared Ontario terms and accessibility evidence were applied to six direct-HLS records. Caption availability is now recorded as available in English, sign-language as source-dependent, and audio description remains unknown; full live-stream reuse still needs written clarification.

Focused health report covered the 26 entries without retained validation history. Validation history now covers all 86 catalogue records; four official pages returned errors from this environment and Jalisco returned an HLS sample-variant warning, which remain visible as review evidence.

Official evidence updated Scottish Parliament TV, Senedd TV, Northern Ireland Assembly TV, and BC Legislature accessibility notes. Captions remain unchanged in aggregate, sign-language unknowns fell from 77 to 71, and audio-description remains unknown for all records.

Tweede Kamer live-debate and Debat Direct evidence now supports source-dependent Dutch Sign Language coverage across the three Tweede Kamer records while preserving caption availability and unknown audio-description status.
Council copyright rules cover audiovisual webcasts under attribution, no-distortion, change-disclosure, and third-party-material conditions.
EU Audiovisual Service/EBS FAQ says material is free of charge for EU-related information and educational purposes, while item-specific restrictions still apply.
UN Web TV copyright guidance says UN video/audio is not public domain and requires authorization plus a licence agreement for use.
OSCE copyright policy requires prior written permission for reproducing, transmitting, broadcasting, or otherwise exploiting content beyond narrow personal/educational written-content use.
Bavarian Landtag livestream/archive guidance requires prior approval for reproduction, use, or publication of video files or parts of them in other publications or online.
Corts Valencianes legal notice authorizes non-commercial reproduction of text and multimedia elements when integrity is preserved and source is mentioned, subject to item-specific restrictions.
Assembly ownership rules confirm source ownership and prohibit editing or commercialization without prior assent, but do not clearly authorize third-party live playback.
Hellenic Parliament terms allow republication of parts of portal content under attribution/integrity conditions, but do not clearly authorize full third-party live-stream playback.

Senate legal notice and broadcasting rules support informational use/reproduction of Senate multimedia and parliamentary speeches under attribution, integrity, no-advertising, logo/source-context, and justified-information-purpose conditions.

For the current proof of concept, technically public HLS remains sufficient for native client-side playback unless recorded rights evidence requires link-out; pending direct streams stay visibly permission-pending rather than being silently demoted.

Speaker guidelines grant conditional permission to replay Hansard webcast video for education, private study, research, criticism, review, and newspaper summary; broadcasters may use excerpts for fair and accurate reports.
Parliament web-use rules prohibit reproduction or distribution of portal material without prior express consent and require prior conformity for links.
General website permissions exist, but audiovisual-material rights questions are directed to Council of Europe audiovisual contacts.
House Broadcasts page is information-purpose only; OpenMB reuse terms were not confirmed to cover legislative audio/video.
Official proceedings page and rules document broadcast access and captions, but not third-party playback or redistribution permission.

reports/review-queues-2026-08-19-rights-next.json groups the remaining 32 pending entries into likely written clarification, keep-pending-after-dated-search, and stricter-policy direct-playback review lists; there are no remaining public-terms follow-up entries.

Congress legal notice allows reuse with attribution/integrity conditions; FAQ says the institutional signal is distributed free to media and citizens and archived videos may be downloaded and used freely after sessions.

recommended_order: Use reports/review-queues-2026-08-19-rights-next.json as the rights execution queue.
Send written-clarification requests for likely_needs_written_clarification entries, starting with Ontario/Nunavut, Norway, Germany, Netherlands, India, Israel, and Council of Europe/PACE.
Keep dated-search pending entries visible under the prototype opt-out playback policy unless source owners publish clearer terms or a stricter post-POC policy is adopted.
For accessibility, start with sources that already claim captions or interpretation in the catalogue, then replace unknown fields only with cited official evidence.
